text:
Alex W: Heads up — I'm seeing a noisy steering signal causing some tier-A customers to get routed through 3+ regions in one request window. Not full fallback loops (yet) but high path churn.

Priya R: That's bad. Any pattern on model variants?

Alex W: Yes — variant compatibility checks are flapping because telemetry weights are spiking for short-lived errors. The router then aggressively reweights and sends traffic to auxiliary regions.

Jamie L: Can you paste a short example trace?

Alex W: Sure (sanitized):

```
request_id=abc123
initial: us-east -> model:v1
fallback: eu-west -> model:v1-quant
fallback2: ap-south -> model:v2-compat
latency: 320ms -> 180ms -> 410ms
```

Dan S: So it's not a single region outage, it's weight oscillation + variant incompatibility causing multipart fallbacks.

Sasha M: I think the problem is the epoch decay on the steering weights is too short (30s). When a single token error skews the KPI, weights flip. We should add smoothing and a max-hop guard.

Priya R: Agreed on smoothing. Also we lack a hard cap on cross-region hop count. We should enforce max_hops=2 for tier-A until we stabilize.

Alex W: Proposal: quick rollback plan + two short patches: 1) server-side emergency change to routing policy: max_hops=2, ignore transient single-sample spikes, 2) patch variant-compatibility to prefer downward-compatible variants instead of arbitrarily different archs.

Jamie L: Can infra tolerate a hot-patch to policy? What about testing?

Dan S: We can push a rollout with a quick circuit-breaker flag: routing.max_hops=2 scoped to customer_tier in the control plane. Test on 5% of tier-A first.

Sasha M: Also adding a per-request hop_count field and short-circuit if hop_count>max_hops — easiest defensive change in the runtime.

InfraBot: deploy check: control-plane flag change requires config schema bump. Recommend feature-flagged rollout via gray release.

Priya R: UX ask for Console: add a small indicator on customer route page showing recent hop distribution and last steering weight change (with a link to traces). That will help SRE and CSMs triage.

Alex W: Agree. For immediate mitigation I'm going to open an emergency PR with: max_hops=2 + smoothing window to 5m + add hop_count short-circuit. Then we can run 5% canary for 15m and monitor.

Jamie L: Also add telemetry metric: routing.hop_count.percentile and routing.steer_entropy per-customer. We don't currently surface entropy.

Sasha M: I'll add a Grafana panel for those metrics under the tier-A dashboard.

Dan S: One more: make fallback preference deterministic order: same-region variants first, then same-region quantized, then cross-region. Removes some randomness.

Priya R: Sounds good. Who owns roll back if the hot-patch breaks?

Alex W: Oncall (cc @oncall) will be primary for rollback, Dan will own the patch PR, Sasha will validate dashboards, Jamie will monitor variant-compat logs.

oncall: Acknowledged. I'll watch the canary and ready to flip the feature flag.

InfraBot: Incident note draft: "Transient steering weight oscillations caused cross-region path churn for a subset of tier-A customers. Mitigation: temporary max_hops=2, smoothing window increased, deterministic fallback order. Follow-up: add entropy metrics and console route visibility."

Alex W: Thanks all — pushing emergency PR now. Please notify partner success for any customer-facing comms if we see user impact. :pray:
